messages:
tessa: Heads-up — since ~08:12 UTC we're seeing degradations on hosted routing for text-gen in us-east-2. Some requests are being rerouted and p95 latency for routed traffic is ~1.8s. Opening incident thread. https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1865033333
omar: oncall. initial triage shows routing-controller retries doubling after intermittent tcp timeouts to the us-east-2 edge. I put a soft throttle on low-priority routes and enabled nearest-region fallback for critical customers. Error spike down from ~5.6% -> ~1.6%.
lee: looking at network team notes — there was a config push to the edge lb earlier that removed a health-check path; unhealthy backend churn caused extra retries. prepping a quick config revert to restore the health-check.
ops-bot: monitor: edge-lb-unhealthy alert firing for us-east-2 (id=edge-1122).
deploy-bot: infra: rolling edge-lb-config revert in us-east-2, batch 1/1, sha=b7c3d9. CI: https://ci.redwood/build/8249
omar: after revert p95 for routed requests back to ~420ms and error rate ~0.4%. leaving throttles on for 15 more minutes while we validate.
support: sent interim update to impacted hosted customers: "We're investigating routing degradations in us-east-2. We've applied fallbacks and reverted an edge config; services are recovering. We'll follow up with timeline and RCA."
tessa: mitigation checklist: 1) throttle low-priority routes (done), 2) enable nearest-region fallback (done), 3) revert edge-lb config (done), 4) monitor for 30m (in progress), 5) customer comms (done). status doc: https://go.redwood/incident/1865033333/summary
lee: scheduling a postmortem to cover config gating and add a preflight health-check test to CI. assigning follow-ups: infra to add CI assertion, routing to add circuit-breaker on retries.
tessa: marking severity=SEV3. i'll assemble exec note after we hit stable metrics for 60m. if anyone sees regressions react with :loud_sound: or DM.
